Latin-transliterated stretch 40:47-59:51 and 1:02:24-1:02:27 (his verb tables, sentences). English-only stretches: 13:29-15:22, 23:12-24:24, 28:57-29:25, 31:32-35:23 (meaning discussion of خرب/خرّب), 47:01-49:11 (meta about the AI form). Pronunciation skipped per S4: قربان for خربان 10:55, jumla/jumleh 22:17-22:37, banbesit/bazaj (dropped ع) 58:22-58:54, روز for رز, charbi/charbu (shadda) 44:57, telefonic 44:13. Asked-then-answered grammar (not errors): بيكون/أكون 05:57, يخربوا? 25:49, bakharreb/bakharraab 40:47, bitkharbi/bitkharibi 40:58, form II past 35:56/36:19. rows.medi_said: Review. What was the word for review?
rows.amal_said: As a noun it's مراجعة. So what is it as a verb? ... صح، براجع.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for the word, she supplied noun مراجعة and verb براجع.

rows.medi_said: اليوم، مم؟ اليوم يوم الـ، جمع
rows.why: Day name came out as جمع (plural) not الجمعة; she moved on to the date (her 'قد' looks like a cut 'قديش'); may be a transcript cut.

rows.medi_said: آآآ، الشمال الـ، روسيا the, the north of Russia. الشمال.
rows.why: Idafa: first word never takes el-; he put الـ on شمال and again on روسيا, she recast to شمال روسيا.

rows.medi_said: الشمال الـ، روس شمال؟ Did you say? رو... شس...
rows.why: Same idafa error repeated 30 s after her first fix; she recast it a second time.

rows.medi_said: Okay. الشمال روس بيكون ... برد كتير ويكون بيمطر أو بتثلج.
rows.why: Third time with el- on the first idafa word (and روس clipped for روسيا); she let it pass this time.
rows.english: The north of Russia is very cold and it rains or snows

rows.medi_said: آآآ ومغني نوع مغيمة.
rows.why: مغني (singer) is a different word from مغيمة (cloudy); he wavered then she recast 'الدنيا ... مغيمة وعتمة'. Sheet: 'it's cloudy | M8ayyme | مغيمة'.

rows.medi_said: شو أكتر، شو أكتر كلمة عندي؟
rows.why: أكتر (more) used for 'what else / what other word'; Levantine wants شو كمان or كلمة تانية. Sheet: 'also / more / too | Kamaan | كمان', 'else/other | taani | تاني'. She did not react.
rows.english: What other word do I have?

rows.medi_said: How do I say dark again؟
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked, she supplied عتمة. Sheet: 'darkness | 3etme | عتمة'.

rows.medi_said: Is it Asafa؟ Is that, is that stars؟
rows.why: He offered عاصفة (storm) for 'stars'; she said No, it is storm, then led him to نجمة/نجوم. Sheet: 'storm | 3aasefe | عاصفة', 'star | Nejme | نجمة'.

rows.medi_said: is it أنجم؟ I don't know. أنجم، نجوم،
rows.why: Invented plural أنجم for نجمة; he also offered نجوم and she picked it (near self-fix).

rows.medi_said: الـ المدينة حوالين or الـ المدينة سان فرانسيسكو Oakland
rows.why: English 'or' dropped inside an Arabic sentence he was building; sheet: 'or | Aw | أو | aw'. She let it pass.
rows.english: the city around (me), or the city San Francisco / Oakland

rows.medi_said: قريب، قريبًا ... مني.
rows.amal_said: What's the، what's-- وشو جمع غريب؟ ... غراب.
rows.why: Cities (plural) need the plural adjective قراب; he used singular قريب (and MSA قريبًا), she asked for the plural and supplied قراب, he repeated 'قراب مني'.

rows.medi_said: الـ المدينة حوالين or الـ المدينة سان فرانسيسكو Oakland
rows.why: Subject is plural (she then demanded plural قراب) but he said singular المدينة; she fixed only the adjective.

rows.medi_said: نعيد ... بنعيد ... بنعيد.
rows.amal_said: قبل ما نزيد بيه، شو بنقيم؟
rows.why: She said بنقيم (we remove) at 11:10; he echoed it as بنعيد (we repeat/return) three times until she re-asked 'شو بنقيم؟' - looks like a mis-hearing of her word, so kept apart as listening.

rows.medi_said: تحت الكلمة.
rows.why: She asked how to say 'the end of the word'; he said تحت (under); she prompted 'The end' and he produced آخر الكلمة which she confirmed. Sheet: 'down / under | Ta7t | تحت', 'last / the end of | 2aa5er | آخر'.

rows.medi_said: آآآ، مزيد.
rows.why: 'we add' came out as مزيد (no b-/her bn- prefix); she had just modelled بنزيد and only said مم. May be transcript.

rows.medi_said: آآآ، ع الـ-- أول الكلمة. ... الأول الـ-- فعل الكلمة.
rows.why: He put الـ (عالأول) before the first idafa word; she said لا and gave أول الكلمة; he still said الأول الـ فعل الكلمة after.

rows.medi_said: means to make something stop working.
rows.amal_said: مم. It's not بخرّب yet. It's بخرب.
rows.wrong: بخرب = to make something stop working
rows.right: بخرب = it/I stop working (get broken); بخرّب = make it stop working
rows.why: He gave the make-X (form II) meaning for the get-X form بخرب; she said it is not بخرّب yet.
rows.english: I stop working / it breaks down

rows.medi_said: آآآ، هي خربات.
rows.why: Past-tense she-ending said as -aat instead of -at (خربت); she recast.
rows.english: she broke down / it (f) stopped working

rows.medi_said: خربوا. It's خربات or خربات؟ خربات. خربات. خربوا.
rows.why: He repeated the -aat she-form after her fix; she recast خربت again.

rows.medi_said: with AC, can I say that? Air conditioning. تباي.
rows.amal_said: مم. تبعيت. We don't-- We haven't discussed تبعيت a lot yet. So تبعيت.
rows.why: Possessive 'mine' built as تباي; she gave the feminine possessive form تبعيت(ي) (تبع + -t + ending). Not on her sheet.

rows.medi_said: صححته.
rows.why: صحّح (to correct) is a different verb from صلّح (to fix/repair); she recast and he repeated صلحته. Not on her sheet.

rows.medi_said: [his Arabic sentence untranscribed 19:11-20:06] because ... (20:34) I said it stops working.
rows.amal_said: بس still هذا الفعل الثاني. ... not بخرّب. بخرب that would be.
rows.why: She flagged he used 'the second verb' (make-X, doubled middle) while he meant 'it stops working' (get-X); his Arabic is not transcribed, the exchange 20:11-20:40 proves it.
rows.english: Everything my fiancee uses stops working

rows.medi_said: Um, [speaking Arabic] ... (21:19) oh, that's right, it's she and not you.
rows.why: Verb must match its subject (she = my fiancee); she recast بتستعمل twice (20:58, 21:13) and at 21:19 he says 'it's she and not you' - so he had the you-f form.

rows.medi_said: Um, [speaking Arabic]
rows.amal_said: So it's, it's, it's just إشي. Everything my girlfriend, my fiancée uses. So it's one thing.
rows.why: She corrected 'everything' to كل إشي ('it's one thing'), implying he used a plural/other noun after كل; his line is untranscribed.

rows.medi_said: Uh, but [speaking Arabic] oh, that's right, it's she and not you. [speaking Arabic]
rows.why: Object كل إشي is fronted, so the verb needs the pointer ending -ه; she recast بتستعمله and later gave the full 'كل إشي بتستعمله بيخرب'.

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic] ... Yeah, [speaking Arabic]
rows.amal_said: بس. بيخرب. بس بيخرب. ... كل إشي بتستعمله بيخرب.
rows.why: He asked 'Do I need to do it for this verb too?' and then attached something to بيخرب; she said 'بس بيخرب' - the second verb takes no ending.

rows.medi_said: okay. [speaking Arabic]
rows.why: On the repeat of the sentence she again recast the last verb to بيخرب; his form is not transcribed.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما تفتحي. ... ما بهتي، ما بهتي. بي-- بتفتحي
rows.why: In 'إذا ما ...' the negated present keeps its b-; he dropped it (ما تفتحي), she said 'With B' and modelled ما بتحطي.
rows.english: if you don't put (it in the fridge)

rows.medi_said: ما بهتي، ما بهتي. بي-- بتفتحي
rows.why: فتح (open) used for حط (put) in 'if you don't put it in the fridge'; she recast ما بتحطي. Sheet: 'put | 7ott | حط', 'open | Efta7 | افتح'.

rows.medi_said: إذا ما بتفتحي، هي الثلاجة.
rows.why: Final version of the sentence still has فتح (open) where حط (put) was intended and she had just modelled it; she said ممتاز.
rows.english: if you don't put (it in) the fridge

rows.medi_said: هي الثلاجة.
rows.why: No preposition before الثلاجة ('in the fridge'); هي may be a transcript of في, so low.

rows.medi_said: Uh, تاكلي. إلي، إلي. خخخ عشان راح يخرب.
rows.why: 'don't forget to eat it' - the object should ride on the verb (تاكليه); he said تاكلي then a separate إلي; she let it pass.
rows.english: don't forget to eat it because it will go bad

rows.medi_said: [يضحك] لازم. اه، خرب
rows.amal_said: عزومة is feminine or masculine؟ ... خربت.
rows.why: العزومة is feminine so the verb is خربت; he said خرب, she asked the gender and supplied خربت.

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic]
rows.amal_said: ما؟ ... ما it didn't come. ... ما أجا.
rows.why: She recast his 'it didn't come' to ما أجا; his attempt is untranscribed. Sheet: 'he came | huwwe aja | هو إجا'.

rows.medi_said: Uh, ثانورك.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. تنورة is skirt. ... فستانك. صح.
rows.why: تنورة (skirt) given for 'dress'; she said Mm-mm, تنورة is skirt, he then found فستانك. Sheet: 'dress | Fus6aan | فستان', 'skirt | Tannoora | تنورة'.

rows.medi_said: غرفةك.
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. يلا أعطيني إنت دورك هلأ.
rows.why: Feminine غرفة takes -t before the possessive ending (غرفتك); transcript shows غرفةك; she let it pass (may be transcript spelling).

rows.medi_said: خربت الغرف بغلط. بالغلط.
rows.why: الغرف is the plural; he meant 'the room'; she only confirmed بالغلط. Could be a dropped ة.
rows.english: I messed up the room by accident

rows.medi_said: شو خرب? ... Uh, جلايك.
rows.why: Feminine جلاية needs -t before the ending: جلايتك; she prompted 'جلاية؟' and he fixed it, she confirmed.

rows.medi_said: مش قصدهم إنّه...
rows.amal_said: مش، مش أزتم or it's past also. ... (42:48) ممتاز.
rows.why: 'They didn't mean' is past, needs كان; she prompted 'it's past also', he reached ما كان قصدهم, she said ممتاز.

rows.medi_said: Uh, مش كان and, uh, مش...
rows.amal_said: Not مش. [تضحك] If you use كان. Not كان.
rows.why: Verbs (كان) take ما, not مش; she said 'Not مش' and he fixed to ما كان.

rows.medi_said: uh, kharabu.
rows.amal_said: So، في عندنا خلاص ما كان is a verb. Because كان and then the verb after it should be what؟ ... صح.
rows.why: After ما كان قصدهم the next verb is bare present (يخرّبوا), not past خرّبوا; she prompted, he produced yecharbu, she said صح.
rows.english: they didn't mean to mess up your work

rows.medi_said: Il, iljao sh-- Iljao shoub. ... Iljao shoub, uh,
rows.why: As a subject phrase 'the hot weather' the adjective keeps el- (الجو الشوب); his الجو شوب reads as the sentence 'the weather is hot'; she recast الشوب, he then said iljao ilshoub bicharrab telefonic and she said ممتاز.
rows.english: the hot weather ruins my phone

rows.medi_said: it would be echarrab, echarrbi. ... So echarrab, echarr, no? No, so charrab.
rows.amal_said: So it's بخرررب. There is a double medal here. ... No. خرب. ... When do I not put the a in command؟
rows.why: Command of a doubled-middle verb takes no initial i-; she said No, gave خرّب and named the rule (no 'a' when the middle is doubled / two consonants).

rows.medi_said: ma tikharrabi, ma tikharrabi, uh, akhliti.
rows.why: 'my food' is masculine أكل + -i = أكلي; he inserted a -t (akhliti) as if feminine; she let it pass. Sheet: 'food | Akel | أكل'.

rows.medi_said: um, yikharabu. ... Keeps, uh, yikharabu?
rows.right: بضلوا بيخربوا (my reading; her recast untranscribed)
rows.why: After بضلوا (they keep) the second verb keeps its b- (بيخربوا); she said no and recast (untranscribed); he repeated yikharabu.
rows.english: why do your keys keep breaking?

rows.medi_said: bitakhra- bitakhar- bitakhrobi. Bitakhrib.
rows.why: 'Did you break them?' is past; he gave present بتخربي, she prompted 'Did you?', he said 'Oh, past tense' and produced kharabtihum, she confirmed.

rows.medi_said: sawarna kharab. Uh, ... were ruined. Kharabu. No. Kha-- uh, khar- kharabu. Kharabu.
rows.amal_said: Which, which one is it؟ [speaks Arabic] ... (55:07 Medi: I knew that.)
rows.right: صورنا خربت (my reading; her line untranscribed)
rows.why: 'Our photos were ruined': verb must agree with صور (non-human plural takes feminine singular خربت); he wavered خرب/خربوا, she asked 'which one is it' and supplied it (untranscribed), he said 'I knew that'.

rows.medi_said: rah bit-- uh, b-- rah bit kh--
rows.why: He started a b- verb after راح; her 'نوبي' is 'no b' - راح takes the bare verb; he then said rah titkharabi.

rows.medi_said: rah yitkhar-- rah titkharabi. ... Yeah, rah titkharabi. Rah atkharabt. ... Uh, rah titkharabiha.
rows.amal_said: ليش؟ You would ruin it? ... No two T. Why two Ts؟ شوربة is feminine. So... one T. ... اه، راح تخربيها.
rows.why: 'You (f) will ruin it (the soup)' is form II تخرّبي + -ها; his titkharabi has the extra t- of the get-ruined form ('No two T'), and the object ending was missing until she asked 'You would ruin it?'.
rows.english: if you put too much salt in the soup, you will ruin it

rows.medi_said: rah yikhrab.
rows.amal_said: Yes, بس we're talking about شوربة. So... (57:42) صح.
rows.why: شوربة is feminine so 'it will go bad' is راح تخرب; he used masculine يخرب, she prompted, he said rah tikhreb, she said صح.
